lessons.title: Linguistic diversity and dialects
lessons.anelcac: Notions of linguistic diversity, dialects, names of languages, geographical classification
objectives: Becoming aware of the linguistic diversity of Cameroon (about 280 languages according to the LACAGEO Mini-Atlas)
Distinguish language, dialect and variant according to academic definitions
Naming Ghomala' and locating it in the geographical classification of the languages of Cameroon
Adopt an attitude of respect towards all languages

teacher.intro: Lesson: Linguistic diversity and dialects. Module: Module I — Cameroonian linguistic diversity.
steps: **Setting the context:** Display the map of the Linguistic Mini-Atlas of Cameroon. Ask students which languages are spoken in their family.
**Exploration:** Have students read the definitions in the Mini-Atlas (language, dialect, patois, national language). Locate Ghomala' in its linguistic region.
**Conceptualisation:** Explain the language / dialect distinction with examples: the Bulu, Ewondo, Eton and Mangisa dialects all belong to the Beti-Fang language (Mini-Atlas).
**Application:** Complete a table: name of the language, family, main region, ISO code.
**Assessment:** Each student gives an oral presentation of Ghomala', indicating family and region.
teacher.freedom: The LACAGEO Mini-Atlas (2013) distinguishes about 280 living languages in Cameroon. The exact number varies according to the criteria (SIL: 274, Ethnologue: 279). Value all the languages cited.
teacher.tips: The LACAGEO Mini-Atlas (2013) distinguishes about 280 living languages in Cameroon. The exact number varies according to the criteria (SIL: 274, Ethnologue: 279). Value all the languages cited.

student.intro: Cameroon is one of the richest nations in the world in languages — the linguistic Mini-Atlas lists about 280! In this lesson, you discover the place of Ghomala' in this great family.
activities: Look at the Mini-Atlas map and find the area where Ghomala' is mainly spoken.
Copy and complete: Ghomala' belongs to the ___ family. It is mostly spoken in the ___ region.
According to the Mini-Atlas, how many living languages are there in the Ghomala' region? Note down this number.
Survey: ask an adult the name of the language in which they were raised and where it is spoken.
Memorise: **dialect** = an intelligible variant of the same language; **national language** = language of an ethnic group that does not extend beyond the borders of one State (ACA LAN).
student.memo: Cameroon has about **280 languages** according to the LACAGEO Mini-Atlas. Ghomala' belongs to a Cameroonian language family and has its own dialectal variants. According to the ACA LAN, a national language is the language of an ethnic group that does not extend beyond the borders of one State.

lessons.title: Classification of languages and linguistic atlas
lessons.anelcac: Classification of the languages of Cameroon: linguistic areas, families, ALCAM atlas
objectives: Name the main linguistic areas of Cameroon
Read and interpret an extract from a linguistic atlas (ALCAM / Mini-Atlas)
Classify Ghomala' according to its typological criteria
Producing a short text presenting Ghomala'

teacher.intro: Lesson: Classification of languages and linguistic atlas. Module: Module I — Cameroonian linguistic diversity.
steps: **Setting the context:** Go back over the definitions. How many language families do students remember?
**Presentation:** The 8 world language families according to Ethnologue (Niger-Kordofanian, Nilo-Saharan, Afro-Asiatic…). Place Cameroonian languages within this whole.
**Explanation:** Show how to find Ghomala' in the ALCAM: ISO code, family, location.
**Guided practice:** In pairs, students find 3 languages neighbouring Ghomala' and note their ISO codes.
**Production:** 5-line paragraph presenting Ghomala' (family, region, speakers, distinctive feature).
teacher.freedom: The online ALCAM is on the Mozilla Data Collective. The LACAGEO Mini-Atlas covers all the administrative regions with maps and statistics.
teacher.tips: The online ALCAM is on the Mozilla Data Collective. The LACAGEO Mini-Atlas covers all the administrative regions with maps and statistics.

student.intro: A linguistic atlas is a specialised map. The ALCAM (Atlas of the Languages of Cameroon) and the LACAGEO Mini-Atlas let you locate Ghomala' precisely.
activities: On the Mini-Atlas map, locate Ghomala' and note its administrative region.
List 3 languages whose area is adjacent to that of Ghomala'.
Classify these 4 languages in a table: Language | Family | Main region.
Write an introductory paragraph about Ghomala' with at least 5 pieces of information taken from the atlas.
Memorise: **ISO 639** = international language codes; **ALCAM** = Atlas des Langues du Cameroun.
student.memo: The **ALCAM** and the **LACAGEO Mini-Atlas** list and locate all the national languages of Cameroon. Cameroon has 8 main language families. Ghomala' appears there with its family and its location. Knowing how to read a linguistic atlas is reading the history of peoples.

lessons.moduleTitle: Module II — Segmental phonology: vowels and consonants
lessons.title: Vowels of Ghomala'
lessons.anelcac: AGLC vowels — simple, specific, complex
objectives: Identify the simple vowels of the phonological system of Ghomala'
Recognising specific vowels absent from French
Pronouncing vowels correctly in the context of a word
Transcribing words containing vowels according to AGLC

teacher.intro: Lesson: Ghomala' vowels. Module: Module II — Segmental phonology: vowels and consonants.
steps: **Setting the context:** Write known words in Ghomala' on the board and ask which sounds students hear.
**Presentation:** Introduce the AGLC. Write the simple vowels of Ghomala' on the board, articulating them clearly.
**Explanation:** Vowels specific to Ghomala' that are absent from French (nasal, particular openness…). Listening and repetition exercises.
**Application:** List of 10 words — students underline the vowels and indicate: simple or specific.
**Assessment:** Dictation of 5 simple words — students transcribe them with the correct vowels.
teacher.freedom: Use the examples from the platform's ALCAM vocabulary. For each specific vowel, give a memorable key word.
teacher.tips: Use the examples from the platform's ALCAM vocabulary. For each specific vowel, give a memorable key word.

student.intro: Every language has its own sounds. In Ghomala', some vowels do not exist in French. This lesson teaches you to hear, pronounce and write them.
activities: Listen to the recordings of the Ghomala' vocabulary and identify the vowels you hear.
Classify the vowels: **Shared with French** | **Specific to Ghomala'**.
Transcribe the 5 dictated words, taking care to note each vowel correctly.
Find 3 words in Ghomala' for each specific vowel and write them down.
Memorise: **AGLC** = Alphabet Général des Langues Camerounaises, the official reference.
student.memo: The vowel system of **Ghomala'** includes simple vowels and specific vowels (e.g. nasalised vowels). They are written using the **AGLC**. Mastery of vowels is the basis of reading and writing in Ghomala'.

lessons.moduleTitle: Module II — Segmental phonology: vowels and consonants
lessons.title: Ghomala' consonants and written production
lessons.anelcac: Consonants — simple, specific, complex; written production of vowels and consonants
objectives: Identify the consonant system of Ghomala'
Recognising specific consonants absent from French
Articulate consonants correctly in context
Writing words with vowels and consonants correctly notated

teacher.intro: Lesson: Ghomala' consonants and written production. Module: Module II — Segmental phonology: vowels and consonants.
steps: **Setting the context:** Recall the vowels. What is a consonant?
**Presentation:** Table of Ghomala' consonants according to the AGLC. Stress the specific consonants (labio-velars, prenasalised, implosives…).
**Explanation:** Articulating difficult consonants: in isolation → syllable → word.
**Application:** Minimal pairs: listening to words that differ only by one consonant.
**Production:** 5 simple sentences in Ghomala' with careful consonant transcription.
teacher.freedom: Implosive and prenasalised consonants are often the most difficult for students who learned to read and write in French. Repeat the listening activities many times.
teacher.tips: Implosive and prenasalised consonants are often the most difficult for students who learned to read and write in French. Repeat the listening activities many times.

student.intro: After the vowels, here are the consonants of Ghomala'! Some are unique — you will only hear them in Ghomala' and in a few neighbouring African languages.
activities: Listen to the minimal pairs and tick the word you hear (e.g. bìlí / pìlí).
Transcribe 5 dictated words, paying attention to the specific consonants.
Find in the vocabulary all the words containing a prenasalised consonant. How many do you find?
Compose 3 simple sentences in Ghomala', each with at least one specific consonant.
Memorise: **minimal pair** = two words identical except for one phoneme.
student.memo: The consonant system of **Ghomala'** includes consonants shared with French and specific consonants (implosives, prenasalised, labio-velars…). Writing them according to the **AGLC** is essential for reading and writing.

lessons.title: Definition and functions of tones
lessons.anelcac: Tones — definition, function, presentation; simple tones (high, low, mid)
objectives: Define tone as a distinctive feature of tone languages
Distinguish lexical tone from grammatical tone
Identify the simple tones of Ghomala'
Transcribing words with their tones according to AGLC

teacher.intro: Lesson: Definition and function of tones. Module: Module III — Suprasegmental phonology: tones.
steps: **Setting the context:** Say two Ghomala' words that are written the same but have different tones and different meanings.
**Presentation:** Define tone. Present the simple tones of Ghomala' and their AGLC diacritics.
**Explanation:** Simple tones: high (´), low (`), mid (¯). Have students repeat each tone.
**Application:** Match recorded words with their tone notation.
**Assessment:** Dictation of 5 words — students note the tones.
teacher.freedom: Singing the tones helps to memorise them. Use a flute or whistle the tonal melodies.
teacher.tips: Singing the tones helps to memorise them. Use a flute or whistle the tonal melodies.

student.intro: Ghomala' is a tonal language: the pitch of your voice changes the meaning of the word! You will learn to hear and write down these tones.
activities: Listen to the pairs of words. For each pair, are the tones the same or different?
Transcribe 5 words with their tones using the AGLC diacritics (´ ` ¯).
Find 2 words in the vocabulary that differ only in tone. What does each one mean?
Sing the tones of a 3-syllable word as High-Low-High, then Low-High-Low. What difference do you hear?
Memorise: high tone = ´ ; low tone = ` ; mid tone = ¯.
student.memo: In **Ghomala'**, tone is phonological: it distinguishes words with different meanings. The **simple tones** are high (´), low (`), and sometimes mid (¯). They are written using the **AGLC** diacritics.

lessons.title: Complex tones and tone-marked written production
lessons.anelcac: Complex tones (rising, falling); finding the tone of a word; tonal written production
objectives: Identify the complex tones of Ghomala' (rising, falling)
Finding the tone of a word by the isolation method
Transcribing sentences with full tone marking
Producing a short text in Ghomala' with correct tones

teacher.intro: Lesson: Complex tones and tonal written production. Module: Module III — Suprasegmental phonology: tones.
steps: **Setting the context:** Recall the simple tones. Announce that some syllables carry two tones in succession.
**Presentation:** Complex tones: falling (̂), rising (̌). Let students hear them and reproduce them.
**Explanation:** Isolation method: say the word with an artificial high tone, then a low one, and listen to which sounds natural.
**Application:** Students find the tone of 10 words in Ghomala' using the isolation method.
**Production:** Dialogue of 6 lines in Ghomala' with complete tone notation.
teacher.freedom: The complex falling tone is often the most frequent. Start with it before the rising tone.
teacher.tips: The complex falling tone is often the most frequent. Start with it before the rising tone.

student.intro: You know the simple tones. Now for the complex tones of Ghomala' — syllables that rise and fall at the same time!
activities: Listen to the recorded words and sort them: Simple tone | Complex tone.
Apply the isolation method to 5 words: say them high, then low, and note the tone you perceive.
Transcribe a dialogue of 4 lines in Ghomala' with all the tones marked.
Write a 3-sentence text in Ghomala' about an action from your daily life, with tone marking.
Memorise: falling tone = ̂ ; rising tone = ̌.
student.memo: The **complex tones** of **Ghomala'** (falling ̂, rising ̌) are melodic movements on a single syllable. The **isolation method** makes it possible to find the tone of an unknown word. A transcription in Ghomala' without tones is incomplete.

lessons.title: The noun base and noun classes
lessons.anelcac: NP: constituents, base noun + affixes, noun classes, personal pronouns
objectives: Identify the structure of the noun in Ghomala' (base + affixes)
Recognising the noun classes of Ghomala'
Form the singular and plural of nouns
Use the personal pronouns corresponding to noun classes

teacher.intro: Lesson: The noun base and noun classes. Module: Module IV — The noun phrase.
steps: **Setting the context:** Write a noun in Ghomala' in the singular and plural. What changes?
**Presentation:** Noun class: in Bantu and Bantoid languages, nouns are grouped into classes marked by prefixes.
**Explanation:** Main noun classes of Ghomala' with singular and plural prefixes.
**Application:** Table: singular → plural for 10 nouns.
**Assessment:** Identify the noun class of 5 nouns.
teacher.freedom: Start from the nouns that students already use. Noun classes often correspond to semantic categories (humans, animals, objects…).
teacher.tips: Start from the nouns that students already use. Noun classes often correspond to semantic categories (humans, animals, objects…).

student.intro: In Ghomala', nouns are organised into **classes**. Each class has its own prefixes for the singular and plural — a much richer system than gender in French!
activities: Using the Ghomala' vocabulary, make a table: Singular | Plural | Noun class.
Identify the class prefix in each noun. Highlight it.
Put the following 5 nouns into the plural by changing the prefix according to the class.
Match each noun with its corresponding class pronoun.
Memorise: **noun class** = grammatical category of nouns, marked by prefixes.
student.memo: In **Ghomala'**, nouns are organised into **noun classes** marked by prefixes. A change of prefix indicates number. Pronouns, adjectives and verbs agree with the class of the noun.

lessons.title: Noun determiners
lessons.anelcac: Determiners: possessives, demonstratives, numerals, indefinites, interrogatives; noun class agreement
objectives: Identify the different types of determiners in Ghomala'
Make determiners agree with the noun according to the noun class
Build complex noun phrases
Producing sentences with complete NPs

teacher.intro: Lesson: Noun determiners. Module: Module IV — The noun phrase.
steps: **Setting the context:** Write a simple noun phrase. How can it be enriched?
**Presentation:** Determiners in Ghomala': possessives, demonstratives, numerals, indefinites, interrogatives.
**Explanation:** Each determiner agrees with the class of the noun (same class prefix or suffix).
**Application:** Complete noun phrases with the correct determiner according to the class.
**Production:** 5 complex noun phrases (noun + 2 determiners) used in sentences.
teacher.freedom: Stress class agreement — one of the most distinctive features of Ghomala' compared with French.
teacher.tips: Stress class agreement — one of the most distinctive features of Ghomala' compared with French.

student.intro: A noun with its determiners becomes much more precise! In Ghomala', determiners agree with the **noun class**.
activities: Complete the NPs with the correct possessive determiner according to the noun class.
Underline the determiners in 5 sentences in Ghomala' and identify their type.
Turn each simple noun phrase into a complex noun phrase by adding a demonstrative and a numeral.
Write 5 sentences in Ghomala' with at least two determiners per noun phrase.
Memorise: **class agreement** = the determiner changes form according to the noun class.
student.memo: In **Ghomala'**, all determiners (possessives, demonstratives, numerals, indefinites, interrogatives) agree with the **noun class** of the noun. A **complex NP** = noun + nominal base + agreeing determiners.

lessons.title: The verb stem and conjugation
lessons.anelcac: VP: constituents, stem, affixes, conjugation, verb tenses
objectives: Identify the verb stem and the conjugation affixes in Ghomala'
Conjugate a verb in the main tenses
Analyse the morphological structure of a verb form
Use verb forms correctly in sentences

teacher.intro: Lesson: The verb stem and conjugation. Module: Module V — The verb phrase.
steps: **Setting the context:** Write a verb form in Ghomala' and ask students to identify the stem.
**Presentation:** Break down a verb form: subject prefix + TAM markers + stem + suffixes.
**Explanation:** Conjugation paradigm of a common verb in Ghomala' in several tenses.
**Application:** Conjugation table: 3 common verbs.
**Assessment:** Translate 5 sentences from French into Ghomala'.
teacher.freedom: The TAM system of Ghomala' is often richer than that of French. Start with the most commonly used tenses.
teacher.tips: The TAM system of Ghomala' is often richer than that of French. Start with the most commonly used tenses.

student.intro: The verb is the heart of the sentence in Ghomala'. It alone carries tense, aspect, mood and subject! In this lesson, you take apart the verbal mechanics.
activities: Break down 5 verb forms in Ghomala': subject prefix | TAM marker | stem | suffix.
Conjugate the verb 'to eat' in Ghomala' in 3 different tenses for all persons.
Identify the tense of 5 sentences in Ghomala' and justify your answer.
Translate 3 sentences from French into Ghomala', taking care with the conjugation.
Memorise: **TAM** = Tense-Aspect-Mood; this is what verbal affixes express in Ghomala'.
student.memo: In **Ghomala'**, a verb form = subject prefix + TAM markers + stem + suffixes. The **TAM** (Tense-Aspect-Mood) system expresses more precise temporal and aspectual nuances than in French.

lessons.title: Verbal moods and negation
lessons.anelcac: Moods: indicative, imperative; negation; written production of simple/complex VP
objectives: Identify and use the main verbal moods of Ghomala'
Form the verbal negation
Build simple and complex verb phrases
Producing a text with a variety of moods and aspects

teacher.intro: Lesson: Verbal moods and negation. Module: Module V — The verb phrase.
steps: **Setting the context:** Give an order in Ghomala'. Which mood is used?
**Presentation:** Moods in Ghomala': indicative, imperative, and other aspectual moods.
**Explanation:** Formation of the negative in Ghomala': prefix, negative suffix, or particle.
**Application:** Turn 5 affirmative sentences into negative ones and vice versa.
**Production:** 8-sentence text alternating affirmation, negation and imperative.
teacher.freedom: Negation in Ghomala' can be double (framing the verb) or simple. Show both cases.
teacher.tips: Negation in Ghomala' can be double (framing the verb) or simple. Show both cases.

student.intro: Giving an order, expressing doubt, denying an action — each nuance has its own form in Ghomala'!
activities: Put the 5 given sentences into the negative form.
Turn these 5 statements into imperatives addressed to a friend.
Identify the mood and polarity (affirmative/negative) of each sentence in the text provided.
Write a dialogue of 6 lines including at least 2 imperatives and 2 negations.
Memorise: **mood** = the way of viewing the action; **negation** = grammatical marker denying the action.
student.memo: In **Ghomala'**, the main moods are the **indicative** and the **imperative**. **Negation** is marked by a particle or a specific affix. The diversity of moods is an expressive richness of Ghomala'.

lessons.moduleTitle: Module VI — The sentence in Ghomala'
lessons.title: The simple sentence and its types
lessons.anelcac: Simple, interrogative, negative and imperative sentence; word order
objectives: Analyse the structure of the simple sentence in Ghomala'
Distinguish the 4 types of sentences
Mastering the order of constituents
Producing varied simple sentences

teacher.intro: Lesson: The simple sentence and its types. Module: Module VI — The sentence in Ghomala'.
steps: **Setting the context:** Read a sentence in Ghomala'. Who does what?
**Presentation:** Basic constituent order in Ghomala'. Compare with French.
**Explanation:** The 4 sentence types from the same basic sentence.
**Application:** Turn declarative sentences into interrogative ones, then into negative ones.
**Production:** 8 varied sentences (2 per type) about school life.
teacher.freedom: Word order in Ghomala' may differ from French. This is a typological feature, not a mistake.
teacher.tips: Word order in Ghomala' may differ from French. This is a typological feature, not a mistake.

student.intro: A well-constructed sentence in Ghomala' follows precise rules. You learn the types of sentences and word order.
activities: Identify the order of constituents in 5 sentences in Ghomala'.
Turn 4 declarative sentences into yes/no questions.
Turn these 4 sentences into negatives.
Write 2 sentences of each type (declarative, interrogative, negative, imperative).
Memorise: the basic order in **Ghomala'** is typologically stable.
student.memo: The **simple sentence** in **Ghomala'** has a characteristic order of constituents. The 4 types (declarative, interrogative, negative, imperative) are formed with specific grammatical markers.

lessons.moduleTitle: Module VI — The sentence in Ghomala'
lessons.title: Logical connectors and the complex sentence
lessons.anelcac: Logical connectors, complex sentence, coordination, subordination; written production
objectives: Identify the logical connectors of Ghomala'
Distinguish coordination from subordination
Build complex sentences
Producing a coherent text with syntactic variety

teacher.intro: Lesson: Logical connectors and the complex sentence. Module: Module VI — The sentence in Ghomala'.
steps: **Setting the context:** Read a short story in Ghomala'. Which words link the sentences?
**Presentation:** Connectors in Ghomala': coordinating and subordinating conjunctions.
**Explanation:** Complex sentence by coordination / by subordination. Examples in Ghomala'.
**Application:** Link 5 pairs of simple sentences with the appropriate connector.
**Production:** 10-sentence text on 'A day in my village' with 5 different connectors.
teacher.freedom: The connectors of Ghomala' often have French equivalents but with different syntactic positions.
teacher.tips: The connectors of Ghomala' often have French equivalents but with different syntactic positions.

student.intro: To tell stories and argue, you need to link your sentences. The **logical connectors** of Ghomala' are your tools!
activities: Underline all the connectors in the text provided.
Classify them: Addition | Cause | Consequence | Opposition | Time.
Link 5 pairs of sentences with the most appropriate connector.
Write a text of 8 sentences with at least 4 different connectors.
Memorise: coordination = same level; subordination = one sentence inside another.
student.memo: In **Ghomala'**, **logical connectors** make it possible to build coherent **complex sentences**. Varying syntactic structures improves the quality of written and spoken expression.

lessons.title: Greeting, introducing yourself and interacting in Ghomala'
lessons.anelcac: Everyday communication situations: greetings, introductions, polite expressions
objectives: Mastering greeting formulas according to context
Introducing yourself and someone else in Ghomala'
Use polite and respectful expressions
Holding a short everyday conversation

teacher.intro: Lesson: Greeting, introducing yourself and interacting in Ghomala'. Module: Module VII — Everyday life (Level 1).
steps: **Setting the context:** Two students meet at the market. Act out the scene in French, then ask how to say it in Ghomala'.
**Presentation:** Greetings in Ghomala' according to the time of day, age and context.
**Explanation:** Formulas of respect towards elders, specific to Ghomala' culture.
**Role play:** In groups of 2, simulate encounters in various contexts (market, school, ceremony).
**Production:** Dialogue of 10 lines between two people of different generations.
teacher.freedom: Greeting rules reflect deep cultural values. Value the knowledge of students from families who speak the language.
teacher.tips: Greeting rules reflect deep cultural values. Value the knowledge of students from families who speak the language.

student.intro: Knowing how to greet in Ghomala' means respecting the culture! The greetings change depending on whom you greet and at what time.
activities: Complete the table of Ghomala' greetings: Time | Formula | Expected response.
Play role A: greeting an elder at the morning market.
Make up a dialogue of 8 lines between a child and their grandfather.
Note down 3 Ghomala' politeness formulas with no direct equivalent in French.
Memorise the morning and evening greeting formulas, and those for elders, in Ghomala'.
student.memo: **Greetings** in **Ghomala'** vary according to the time of day, status and social context. They reflect the community's values of respect and solidarity.

lessons.title: Express everyday needs and actions
lessons.anelcac: Real-life situations: shopping, requests for help, travelling, daily activities
objectives: Express everyday needs in Ghomala'
Describe daily activities
Use vocabulary for places and actions of everyday life
Producing a descriptive text on a typical day

teacher.intro: Lesson: Expressing everyday needs and actions. Module: Module VII — Everyday life (Level 1).
steps: **Setting the context:** Images of scenes from daily life — market, field, school, home. How can they be described in Ghomala'?
**Presentation:** Thematic vocabulary: food, travel, household activities.
**Simulation:** Market scene: buyer and seller in Ghomala'.
**Application:** Describe your day in Ghomala' (from waking up to going to bed).
**Production:** 10-sentence text: 'My day in Ghomala''.
teacher.freedom: Everyday vocabulary is the most motivating. Link the ALCAM words to real situations.
teacher.tips: Everyday vocabulary is the most motivating. Link the ALCAM words to real situations.

student.intro: You know how to greet people. Now you are going to manage in everyday situations in Ghomala': at the market, on the road, at home.
activities: Match each picture of a scene from daily life with the corresponding word or sentence in Ghomala'.
Play the role of the seller at the market: answer the requests in Ghomala'.
Write 5 sentences describing your morning activities from the time you wake up.
Translate these 5 sentences about daily journeys into Ghomala'.
Memorise 10 everyday words in Ghomala' with their French translation.
student.memo: The **everyday** vocabulary in **Ghomala'** covers food, getting around and household activities. Mastering it allows functional communication in all contexts.

lessons.title: Argue and persuade in Ghomala'
lessons.anelcac: Elaborate communication: argumentation, narration, formal speech
objectives: Build a simple argument in Ghomala'
Use the expressions of formal speech
Narrating a past event coherently
Delivering a 2-minute oral speech in Ghomala'

teacher.intro: Lesson: Arguing and persuading in Ghomala'. Module: Module VIII — Everyday life (Level 2).
steps: **Setting the context:** Read a proverb in Ghomala'. Ask students to explain it and defend it.
**Presentation:** Formulas of formal oral speech in Ghomala': forms of address, opening, closing.
**Explanation:** Structure of an argument: thesis → arguments → examples → conclusion.
**Practice:** Debate: for or against the use of Ghomala' at school? Each group defends its position.
**Production:** 2-minute speech on a given theme.
teacher.freedom: Public speaking is highly valued in Cameroonian cultures. Draw on this tradition to motivate the students.
teacher.tips: Public speaking is highly valued in Cameroonian cultures. Draw on this tradition to motivate the students.

student.intro: In Ghomala' cultures, well-spoken words are a force. You learn to argue and persuade with eloquence.
activities: Identify in the text: thesis, arguments, examples.
Prepare 3 arguments to defend the teaching of Ghomala' in primary school.
Give an opening speech for a ceremony in Ghomala'.
Narration: tell in Ghomala' about a memorable event from your school life.
Memorise the opening and closing formulas of a formal speech in Ghomala'.
student.memo: **Argumentation** in **Ghomala'** follows this pattern: thesis → arguments → examples → conclusion. **Formal speech** follows precise cultural conventions. Mastery of elaborate oral expression is a high-level skill.

lessons.title: Oral literature and advanced written production
lessons.anelcac: Oral literature: proverbs, tales, riddles; long written production
objectives: Analyse the structure of a tale or a riddle in Ghomala'
Identify the themes and values conveyed
Writing a short tale following the conventions of the genre
Using oral literature as a teaching resource

teacher.intro: Lesson: Oral literature and advanced written production. Module: Module VIII — Everyday life (Level 2).
steps: **Setting the context:** Tell or play a short tale in Ghomala'.
**Presentation:** Genres of oral literature: tales, proverbs, riddles, epics.
**Analysis:** Structure of the tale: initial situation → disruption → events → resolution → moral.
**Application:** Analyse a tale provided, following this structure.
**Production:** Tale of at least 15 lines in Ghomala' with an explicit moral.
teacher.freedom: Oral literature is a threatened cultural treasure. Invite community storytellers if possible.
teacher.tips: Oral literature is a threatened cultural treasure. Invite community storytellers if possible.

student.intro: Ghomala' tales, proverbs and riddles are literary works in their own right. You will analyse them and you will create your own!
activities: Read the tale provided and identify the 5 stages of its narrative structure.
Identify 3 moral values taught by this tale.
Translate a proverb in Ghomala' into French and explain its figurative meaning.
Write a short tale (15 lines) in Ghomala' with a moral about work or respect.
Memorise: tale = fictional narrative with an educational purpose; proverb = brief formula of collective wisdom.
student.memo: The **oral literature** of **Ghomala'** (tales, proverbs, riddles) transmits the values of the community. The tale has a 5-stage structure. Writing it in Ghomala' draws on all the language skills acquired.

lessons.title: Who are the Ghomala' (Bapa)? Identity, language and territory
lessons.anelcac: Cultural areas, cultural identity, settlement
objectives: Name the Ghomala' (Bapa) community and explain its name
Locating your territory and its neighbours
Telling one's origin according to tradition

vocabulary.frenchText: At the bottom of the tarot fields

lessons.competence: Introduce the Ghomala' (Bapa) community (name, language, territory, neighbours, origin) and place it within the cultural diversity of Cameroon.
lessons.situation: A pen pal from another region asks you to introduce the Ghomala' (Bapa) community to them: who are they, where do they live, where did they come from?
lessons.materiel: Map of Cameroon, cultural profile of the community (“Cultures” section of Likalo).

teacher.intro: Expected competence: Present the Ghomala' (Bapa) community (name, language, territory, neighbours, origin) and place it within the cultural diversity of Cameroon.

steps.title: Discovering the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Write the situation on the board and have it read aloud: “A pen friend from another region asks you to introduce the Ghomala' community (Bapa): who are they, where do they live, where do they come from?” Students think individually.

steps.title: Working on the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Questions to guide the analysis: — What do the Ghomala' (Bapa) call themselves, and what does this name mean? — What language do they speak, and where else is it spoken? — Which peoples do they live alongside? — Where did they come from, according to tradition?

steps.title: Sharing and comparing the results (5 min)
steps.instruction: Compare the groups' answers, keep the correct proposals on the board and identify what the class does not yet know.

steps.title: Mobilising resources (20 min)
steps.instruction: Present the following elements, or have the students discover them: • Majority group, in relation with many neighbours (Batcham, Bana, Baleng…); most Bapa speak several languages. • The speech variety of Bapa is not spoken elsewhere in this form. • Formerly endogamous, the Bapa today marry within and outside the group, men and women alike. • The site, rugged, was not occupied before them; waterfalls, caves and forests make it a true place of pilgrimage, which keeps the authenticity of the West. • The Bapa are said to have come from Batié (another version cites Haut-Nkam); the chiefdoms remain “sisters” and visit each other at major ceremonies.

steps.title: Consolidating what has been learned — written summary (5 min)
steps.instruction: A people of the Hauts-Plateaux, the Bapa (Pepa) settled on a rugged site never occupied before them, rich in waterfalls, caves and sacred forests. A hereditary chiefdom linked to sister chiefdoms such as Batié, a cult of skulls and ancestors, and the great biennial kan festival, where young boys are initiated and shape their identity.

steps.title: Assessment of learning (10 min)
steps.instruction: On a map of Cameroon, locate the Ghomala' (Bapa) community and its neighbours, then write 5 sentences to introduce it to your pen pal.

steps.title: Remediation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Correct together; with students who are struggling, go back over a single element of the written summary, using a concrete example from their own community.

teacher.freedom: Some knowledge (rites, sacred places, initiate societies) is restricted: in class, only what the community makes public is covered, with respect and without judgement. Compare with the students' own culture.
teacher.tips: Approach recommended by the National Cultures teaching guide: active and participatory methods (“learning by doing”). If possible, invite a resource person from the community, or propose a survey of the elders.

lessons.title: Power and social organisation among the Ghomala' (Bapa)

objectives: Identify traditional authorities
Explain how decisions are made
Identifying the rules of deference
lessons.competence: Describe how the Ghomala' (Bapa) organise power, make decisions and regulate community life.
lessons.situation: An important decision has to be made for the whole Ghomala' village (Bapa). Who decides, and how?
lessons.materiel: The community's cultural profile, paper and felt-tip pens for the organisation chart.

teacher.intro: Expected competence: Describe how the Ghomala' (Bapa) organise power, make decisions and regulate community life.

steps.title: Discovering the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Write the situation on the board and have it read out: “An important decision has to be made for the whole village of the Ghomala' (Bapa). Who decides, and how?” The students think about it individually.

steps.title: Working on the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Questions to guide the analysis: — Who holds authority? — How are decisions made (consensus, vote, the chief's decision)? — What rules of respect and deference are observed? — Which groups or societies play a particular role?

steps.title: Sharing and comparing the results (5 min)
steps.instruction: Compare the groups' answers, keep the correct proposals on the board and identify what the class does not yet know.

steps.title: Mobilising resources (20 min)
steps.instruction: Present the following elements, or have the students discover them: • The chiefdoms of the Highlands are linked (politics, cults, festivals); society is hierarchical (chief, notables…). • Decisions originate at the base and rise by stages (neighbourhood, notables, council, chief), by vote and by consensus. • Anyone can meet the chief, regardless of sex or age. • Hereditary succession within the royal family, generally from father to son. • Roles passed down in families: marriage instructors, midwives, healers, specialists in removing skulls, gravediggers.

steps.title: Consolidating what has been learned — written summary (5 min)
steps.instruction: The chiefdoms of the Hauts-Plateaux are linked (politics, cults, festivals); society is hierarchical (chief, notables…). Decisions originate at the base and rise through stages (neighbourhood, notables, council, chief), by vote and by consensus. Anyone can meet the chief, regardless of sex or age.

steps.title: Assessment of learning (10 min)
steps.instruction: Draw a diagram (organisation chart) of power among the Ghomala' (Bapa), then explain in 3 sentences how a decision is made.

steps.title: Remediation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Correct together; with students who are struggling, go back over a single element of the written summary, using a concrete example from their own community.

steps.title: Sharing and comparing the results (5 min)
steps.instruction: Compare the groups' answers, keep the correct proposals on the board and identify what the class does not yet know.

steps.instruction: The Ghomala' (Bapa) eat mainly nkui tubers, yellow sauce with cassava or maize flour. Traditional drinks: raffia wine. These foods are linked to the group's activities and the produce of its environment.

lessons.title: Birth, name and the passage to adulthood among the Ghomala' (Bapa)
lessons.anelcac: Key events: birth, naming, initiation
objectives: Explain the meaning of a birth
Describe how names are given

vocabulary.frenchText: The one who makes no mistakes
The one who has his hands on his neck

lessons.competence: Explain how the Ghomala' (Bapa) welcome a child, give them a name and mark their entry into adulthood.
lessons.situation: A child has just been born into a Ghomala' family (Bapa). How will the child be named, and how will they become an adult?

teacher.intro: Expected competence: Explain how the Ghomala' (Bapa) welcome a child, give them a name and mark their entry into adulthood.

steps.title: Discovering the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Write the situation on the board and have it read out: “A child has just been born into a Ghomala' (Bapa) family. How will he or she be named, and how will he or she become an adult?” The students think about it individually.

steps.title: Working on the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Questions to guide the analysis: — What does a birth mean for the community? — Who gives the name, when and how? — Can the name change during a lifetime? — When and how does one become a man or a woman?

steps.title: Sharing and comparing the results (5 min)
steps.instruction: Compare the groups' answers, keep the correct proposals on the board and identify what the class does not yet know.

steps.title: Mobilising resources (20 min)
steps.instruction: Present the following elements, or have the students discover them: • There are markers for men, women, twins and the child who follows them. • The name depends on the context of the birth, happy or unhappy. • One changes name with each ennoblement, on receiving new titles; the title comes before the name of nobles. • At birth, the priests of the community name the child and reveal their mission. Death is a family and community tragedy; the deceased remains bound to the living. • The boy becomes a man when he can marry, between 20 and 30 years old; the girl, when her body changes and she can run a household.

steps.title: Consolidating what has been learned — written summary (5 min)
steps.instruction: There are markers for men, women, twins and the child who follows them. The name depends on the context, happy or unhappy, of the birth. A person changes name with each ennoblement, on receiving new titles; the title comes before the name of nobles.

student.memo: Among the Ghomala' (Bapa), the traditional dances (kan, sameli, ntchen) accompany the major moments of life: festivals, mourning, weddings, initiations. Instruments: tam-tam, drum, whistle, balafon. Festival(s): kan festival.

lessons.moduleTitle: Module C-IV — Cultural practices in communities (Level I)
lessons.title: Traditional economy and access to land among the Ghomala' (Bapa)
lessons.anelcac: Community practices: traditional economy
objectives: Identify economic activities
Explain the division of tasks
Explain access to land
lessons.competence: Describe the economic activities of the Ghomala' (Bapa), the division of tasks between men and women and the rules of access to land.
lessons.situation: A development project wants to help the Ghomala' (Bapa). First you need to understand how they work and who owns the land.

teacher.intro: Expected competence: Describe the economic activities of the Ghomala' (Bapa), the division of tasks between men and women and the rules of access to land.

steps.title: Discovering the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Write the situation on the board and have it read out: “A development project wants to help the Ghomala' (Bapa). First, we need to understand how they work and who owns the land.” The students think about it individually.

steps.title: Working on the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Questions to guide the analysis: — What are the activities of men? of women? — Who owns the land and how is it accessed? — Which products are sold or exchanged? — Have these activities changed?

steps.title: Sharing and comparing the results (5 min)
steps.instruction: Compare the groups' answers, keep the correct proposals on the board and identify what the class does not yet know.

steps.title: Mobilising resources (20 min)
steps.instruction: Present the following elements, or have the students discover them: • Trade, building, livestock (goats, pigs, poultry), farming. • Land belongs to families and is passed on by inheritance; the heir receives all the property of the deceased. • Varied crafts: bamboo and rattan furniture, thatched roofs, masks, drums and tom-toms, iron objects.

steps.title: Consolidating what has been learned — written summary (5 min)
steps.instruction: Trade, construction, livestock rearing (goats, pigs, poultry), farming. Land belongs to families and is passed down by inheritance; the heir receives all the belongings of the deceased.

steps.title: Assessment of learning (10 min)
steps.instruction: Make a two-column table (men / women) of the activities of the Ghomala' (Bapa), then explain how land is accessed.

steps.title: Remediation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Correct together; with students who are struggling, go back over a single element of the written summary, using a concrete example from their own community.

teacher.freedom: Some knowledge (rites, sacred places, initiate societies) is restricted: in class, only what the community makes public is covered, with respect and without judgement. Compare with the students' own culture.
teacher.tips: Approach recommended by the National Cultures teaching guide: active and participatory methods (“learning by doing”). If possible, invite a resource person from the community, or propose a survey of the elders.

lessons.moduleTitle: Module C-V — Cultural practices in communities (Level II)
lessons.title: Beliefs, sacred places and taboos among the Ghomala' (Bapa)
lessons.anelcac: Community practices: symbolism, rites, taboos
objectives: Explain beliefs about life and death
Identify sacred places
Explain the role of taboos
lessons.competence: Explain the beliefs, sacred places and taboos of the Ghomala' (Bapa), and their role in regulating social life.
lessons.situation: A visitor arrives among the Ghomala' (Bapa). Which places and rules must they absolutely respect?

teacher.intro: Expected competence: Explain the beliefs, sacred places and taboos of the Ghomala' (Bapa), and their role in regulating social life.

steps.title: Discovering the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Write the situation on the board and have it read out: “A visitor arrives among the Ghomala' (Bapa). What places and rules must they absolutely respect?” The students think about it individually.

steps.title: Working on the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Questions to guide the analysis: — What are the beliefs about birth and death? — Which places are sacred, and why? — What are the main taboos, and for whom? — How were serious offences atoned for?

steps.title: Sharing and comparing the results (5 min)
steps.instruction: Compare the groups' answers, keep the correct proposals on the board and identify what the class does not yet know.

steps.title: Mobilising resources (20 min)
steps.instruction: Present the following elements, or have the students discover them: • Cults of skulls, gods, ancestors and God, as among the other Bamileke, especially in the dry season. • Natural sacred places that belong to no family: waterfalls, caves, rocks, sacred forests. • At birth, the priests of the community name the child and reveal their mission. Death is a family and community tragedy; the deceased remains bound to the living. • Taboos: incest, sitting on the chair of one's father's wife. Prohibitions: striking one's parents, stealing in sacred places, eating one's totem animal. • Serious offences: harming the chief's wife, witchcraft, murder, desecration of skulls; these led to expulsion.

steps.title: Consolidating what has been learned — written summary (5 min)
steps.instruction: Cults of skulls, of the gods, of the ancestors and of God, as among the other Bamileke, especially in the dry season. Natural sacred places that belong to no family: waterfalls, caves, rocks, sacred forests.

steps.title: Assessment of learning (10 min)
steps.instruction: Write a short guide to good conduct for a visitor among the Ghomala' (Bapa) (3 places or rules to respect, with the reason for each).

steps.title: Remediation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Correct together; with students who are struggling, go back over a single element of the written summary, using a concrete example from their own community.

teacher.freedom: Some knowledge (rites, sacred places, initiate societies) is restricted: in class, only what the community makes public is covered, with respect and without judgement. Compare with the students' own culture.
teacher.tips: Approach recommended by the National Cultures teaching guide: active and participatory methods (“learning by doing”). If possible, invite a resource person from the community, or propose a survey of the elders.

lessons.moduleTitle: Module C-V — Cultural practices in communities (Level II)
lessons.title: Greeting, introducing yourself and counting in Ghomala'
lessons.anelcac: Traditional media and transmission: everyday language
objectives: Greeting according to the time of day
Introducing yourself
Counting from 1 to 10

vocabulary.frenchText: morning greetings (as a sign of deference/respect)

lessons.competence: Use the greeting and introduction formulas of the Ghomala' (Bapa) and count from 1 to 10, respecting customs.
lessons.situation: You are visiting a Ghomala' (Bapa) family. Greet them, introduce yourself and take part in sharing the kola nuts while counting.
lessons.materiel: Cultural profile (“Common expressions” and “Counting” sections), kola nuts or small objects.

teacher.intro: Expected competence: Use the greeting and introduction formulas of the Ghomala' (Bapa) and count from 1 to 10, respecting customs.

steps.title: Discovering the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Write the situation on the board and have it read aloud: “You are visiting a Ghomala' family (Bapa). Greet them, introduce yourself and take part in the sharing of the kola nuts by counting.” Students think individually.

steps.title: Working on the situation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Questions to guide the analysis: — How do you greet people depending on the time of day? — How do you introduce yourself (name, origin, place of residence)? — How do you count from 1 to 10? Is the system decimal, vigesimal…? — Why is language a tool of transmission?

steps.title: Sharing and comparing the results (5 min)
steps.instruction: Compare the groups' answers, keep the correct proposals on the board and identify what the class does not yet know.

steps.title: Mobilising resources (20 min)
steps.instruction: Present the following elements, or have the students discover them: • The language of the community is Ghomala'. • Greeting formulas: U yoge ntazè A ngèke = Hello (neutral formula, at any time); U liè = morning greeting (one person); Pu yogyele = morning greeting (several people). • Counting from 1 to 5: tchu, pwe, Tan, kwe, Té/ yaté. • The founding chief was called Youdom. • The Bapa likes to live in community and to share joys and sorrows; marriages, mutual aid and development are settled in meetings. The group has managed to preserve its authenticity.

steps.title: Consolidating what has been learned — written summary (5 min)
steps.instruction: Greeting and counting in Ghomala' are the first steps towards communicating with the Ghomala' (Bapa). Polite expressions show the respect owed to people according to the time of day and their rank.

steps.title: Assessment of learning (10 min)
steps.instruction: Role play in pairs: greet each other, introduce yourselves, ask where the other person comes from and count objects from 1 to 10.

steps.title: Remediation (5 min)
steps.instruction: Correct together; with students who are struggling, go back over a single element of the written summary, using a concrete example from their own community.

teacher.freedom: Some knowledge (rites, sacred places, initiate societies) is restricted: in class, only what the community makes public is covered, with respect and without judgement. Compare with the students' own culture.
teacher.tips: Approach recommended by the National Cultures teaching guide: active and participatory methods (“learning by doing”). If possible, invite a resource person from the community, or propose a survey of the elders.

student.intro: Learn to greet, introduce yourself and count in Ghomala'.
